name: Patchline classroom lab kits
claim: Patchline ships classroom lab kits for database, software engineering, programming languages, and DevOps courses. The kits are not slideware: every lab names a real Patchline evidence artifact, an instructor solution gate, the exact reproducing make command, expected generated artifacts, and a negative control that students and instructors can mutate to see the gate fail.

labs.title: Prove a backfill before tightening a NOT NULL contract
labs.student_prompt: Inspect the staged backfill plan, run the instructor gate, and decide whether the contract and compatibility-code deletion can proceed.
objectives: Explain why every pre-existing row needs replay-store evidence before NOT NULL tightening
Distinguish a passing backfill proof from an incomplete-row counterexample

solution_outline: Run the staged backfill planner gate
Inspect the generated JSON for blocked contract stages
Discuss why the incomplete replay store is the negative control

negative_controls.mutation: Use the incomplete replay store so one legacy invoice has no target value.
negative_controls.expected_counterexample: contract and compatibility deletion remain blocked with the missing row witness

labs.title: Review every intermediate state in a migration PR sequence
labs.student_prompt: Review the patch-series spec and explain why a multi-PR migration can fail even when the final schema looks valid.
objectives: Map SQL statement boundaries to invariant checks
Use dependency order and schema hashes to justify escalation

solution_outline: Compare safe and unsafe patch-series fixtures
Explain why documentation alone cannot substitute for intermediate invariant checks

negative_controls.mutation: Swap in the unsafe patch-series fixture that violates an invariant before the final PR.
negative_controls.expected_counterexample: the verifier emits an invariant counterexample before approval

labs.title: Find the path witness that reaches an unsafe repair guard
labs.student_prompt: Run the symbolic execution gate and explain why the vulnerable guard reaches an unsafe leaf while the hardened guard does not.
objectives: Interpret path constraints as a bounded program-analysis proof
Explain why the unsafe witness is a counterexample rather than a test assertion

solution_outline: Contrast the hardened guard's unreachable unsafe leaf

negative_controls.mutation: Remove the lock precondition from the hardened guard.
negative_controls.expected_counterexample: unsafe_reachable becomes true with a witness

courses.title: DevOps: deployment ordering for data changes

labs.title: Prove migration jobs are ordered before dependent deploys
labs.student_prompt: Inspect the infra-ordering evidence and decide whether a migration job can race the application rollout.
objectives: Recognize Helm hook and sync-wave evidence for ordered migrations
Explain why an unordered database job must fail the deployment-ordering gate

solution_outline: Inspect sequenced and unordered job classifications
Connect deploy ordering facts to migration safety

negative_controls.mutation: Remove the Helm hook or sync-wave marker from the migration job.
negative_controls.expected_counterexample: the job is classified as unordered and must not be accepted
